Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0123", "row_sha256": "2519508d29d6d17308ab1612dd1a46bb464a374ed3fdcd50d3d6ae126acf3aff", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "we need a prompt for a document move for harbor operations. the current source is the Dockside Shared Documents library in the old SharePoint site, and the destination is the Harbor Ops team site, which is connected to Teams. this is the archive of monthly site visit reports, not the live working folders. the scope is the eighteen monthly folders from January 2023 through June 2024, inclusive. keep the folder names and their existing month/year order; people recognize them that way, and we should not ask for a new naming scheme. some reports link to inspection photos and follow-up notes, and a few folders have subfolders, so include those in the review rather than treating each month as a flat collection of files.

i want the actual move to happen only if the preflight pilot passes every check. use three representative monthly folders for that pilot: January 2023 because it has several subfolders, September 2023 because it has photo links, and May 2024 because its reports include follow-up notes. for each one check that the files open at the destination, the current access permissions are retained, and links to the photos and notes still resolve after the proposed move. also compare the folder and subfolder counts before and after the pilot and verify the existing names and order. the condition is all of those checks pass for all three pilot folders, not that most of them pass or that someone thinks any problem is minor. don't start moving the other fifteen folders while a pilot check is still unresolved.

if and only if the full pilot passes, move all eighteen monthly folders into the Harbor Ops team site, keeping their names, month/year order, subfolders, and existing permissions. preserve the links to inspection photos and follow-up notes. we are not asking to reorganize the reports, edit their contents, or delete anything from the source during the move. the old library is still used by staff while the migration is being reviewed, and the source copies need to remain available until the new location has been checked. don't describe the move as completed in advance; the prompt should ask for the action conditionally, since nobody has run this pilot yet.

if any one of the pilot checks fails or cannot be confirmed, leave all eighteen folders in the Dockside library and do a different useful task instead: make an exception register for the pilot, naming the affected folder and the check that failed or remains unconfirmed, with a brief description of the issue. don't move only the folders that passed, and don't treat missing evidence as a pass. the team can use that register to decide what to investigate, but don't ask the person doing the work to guess at a fix or change permissions to make the check pass. no archive folder should be moved under this fallback.

for context, the reports are used by coordinators and field staff who may open them from saved links rather than browsing from the site home page. one coordinator said, “I use the old links in the monthly handover notes, so I need to know they still reach the right photos.” the quote is a reason to check links, not a request to rewrite those notes. several folders also inherit access from the old library, so the permission comparison needs to cover what users can actually access, not just whether a folder exists at the destination. don't assume the destination automatically has matching access because it is a team site.

please make the resulting request usable by someone planning and carrying out this migration. keep the scope to the eighteen named months and the three pilot folders described above; do not silently add other years, working folders, or unrelated libraries. state the gate before the move and make the all-checks requirement easy to spot. if the gate fails, the exception register is the alternative task, not an additional move or a partial migration. we have not specified a particular migration tool or a date for carrying out the work, so don't pick one or invent a deadline. the prompt can ask for a concise record of whether the checks passed, but it must not presume an outcome.

1. the pilot checks are file opening, retained permissions, working photo and note links, folder/subfolder counts, and existing names and order.
2. a failed or unconfirmed check means the full move is not authorized; leave all eighteen source folders in place and prepare the exception register instead.

the request should distinguish the pilot from the remaining fifteen folders: the pilot is a check of three representative folders, and a successful result is the condition for moving the complete eighteen-folder set. keep the old source available while the destination is checked, and do not request deletion of the source copies as part of this work. return only the migration prompt, not a migration plan, an exception register, or a claim that anything has already been moved. the end result should still leave the person doing the work with the specific checks, the conditional main action, and the fallback clearly stated. our records manager will review the wording before it is sent to the site team, so it needs to be direct without turning the fallback into the primary task.", "output": "Prepare and carry out the Harbor Operations archive migration described below. The source is the Dockside Shared Documents library in the old SharePoint site; the destination is the Harbor Ops team site connected to Teams. The scope is the eighteen monthly folders containing archived site visit reports, from January 2023 through June 2024, inclusive. Do not include live working folders, other years, or unrelated libraries. Retain the existing folder names and month/year order. Include the folders’ subfolders in the checks and migration.

Before moving the archive, run a preflight pilot using these three representative monthly folders:
1. January 2023, which has several subfolders.
2. September 2023, which has photo links.
3. May 2024, whose reports include follow-up notes.

For each pilot folder, verify all of the following at the destination: files open; existing access permissions are retained; links to inspection photos and follow-up notes resolve after the proposed move; folder and subfolder counts match; and existing names and order are preserved. The move is authorized only if every check passes for all three pilot folders. Do not treat a partial pass, a minor issue, or missing evidence as a pass. Do not begin moving the other fifteen folders while any pilot check is unresolved.

If and only if the complete pilot passes, move all eighteen monthly folders to the Harbor Ops team site. Preserve their names, month/year order, subfolders, existing permissions, and links to inspection photos and follow-up notes. Do not reorganize the reports, edit their contents, or delete the source copies as part of this work. The old library is still used by staff during review, so keep the source copies available until the new location has been checked. Do not report the move as completed before it has taken place.

If any pilot check fails or cannot be confirmed, leave all eighteen folders in the Dockside library. Instead, prepare an exception register that names each affected pilot folder, identifies the check that failed or remains unconfirmed, and briefly describes the issue. Do not move only the folders that passed, move any archive folder under this fallback, guess at a fix, or change permissions to make a check pass. The exception register can support the team’s decision about what to investigate; it does not authorize a partial migration.

Coordinators and field staff sometimes open reports through saved links rather than browsing from the site home page. A coordinator said, “I use the old links in the monthly handover notes, so I need to know they still reach the right photos.” Use this as context for checking links; it is not a request to rewrite the handover notes. Some folders inherit access from the old library, so compare what users can actually access, rather than checking only that a folder exists at the destination. Do not assume the team site automatically has matching permissions.

Ask for a concise record of whether the pilot checks passed, without presuming the result. No migration tool or work date has been specified, so do not select a tool or invent a deadline. Return only the migration prompt; do not produce a migration plan, an exception register, or a claim that anything has already been moved."}]
